replicated_originals.reference: Blackwell, Trzesniewski & Dweck (2007) Implicit theories of intelligence predict achievement across an adolescent transition: A longitudinal study and an intervention
Yeager, Walton, Brady, et al. (2016) Teaching a lay theory before college narrows achievement gaps at scale

A.reason: The paper (titled 'Failure to Replicate') tests a one-time growth mindset intervention on college grades/GPA/credits for first-time college students and disadvantaged subgroups, explicitly targeting the claims attributed to Yeager, Walton et al. (2016): benefits at the transition to college and larger effects for minority, low-income, first-generation students.

B.reason: Ref [5] is the intervention model: the treatment article was 'similar in content to previous mindset interventions (e.g., [5])' (brain grows with effort; math), and math was chosen because [5] addressed it; the study tests whether that intervention improves grades (conceptual/close-extension in a college sample).

notes: The paper never names a single original; it frames itself as a failure to replicate growth-mindset intervention effects generally. Blackwell et al. (2007) is the cited procedural model for the manipulation; Yeager, Walton et al. (2016) is the cited source for the college-transition and disadvantaged-subgroup claims tested. Either could reasonably be judged the sole original; Paunesku et al. (2015, 'Mind-set interventions are a scalable treatment...') is also cited as supporting evidence but not as the model. Replication type is conceptual/close extension (one-time online reading + letter to future student, regional university, math and psychology courses); result: failure (all d near 0).
